description: Raises an error if its first argument is false/nil; otherwise returns all its arguments. Pure language op.

Raises an error with the given message object (any type) and unwinds. level is honored: a string message gets a chunk:line: prefix from the call site level frames up (level 0 = no prefix), via Vm.raiseLocatedError + the shared callSiteAt locator.
Calls a function in protected mode via Vm.callValue; returns true plus results, or false plus the error object. Catchable faults only (OOM/effect-log errors rethrow to protect determinism).
Like pcall but takes a message handler invoked with the error value before the stack unwinds (so debug.traceback inside it sees the error site).
With a number n returns all arguments after the n-th; with '#' returns the count of extra arguments.
Returns the type of its argument as a string (nil/boolean/number/string/table/function/thread/userdata).
Converts any value to a string, honouring the __tostring metamethod (a non-string result errors). __name not yet honoured.

Converts its argument to a number (optionally in a given base), or returns nil/fail. JIT: the no-base string form records on-trace (str2num_i/str2num_f guarded callouts, doc 30); numeric args fold; explicit-base form stays a barrier.
Returns (next, t, nil): a deterministic iterator over all key/value pairs (array part ascending, then hash part in canonical key order).
Returns an iterator over the array part of a table until the first nil.
Primitive table traversal: array part ascending then hash part in canonical key order; underpins pairs and is snapshot-stable.
Compares two values for equality without invoking __eq.
Reads table[index] without invoking __index.
Writes table[index]=value without invoking __newindex; returns the table.
Returns the length of a table or string without invoking __len.
Sets (or removes) the metatable of a table; errors if protected. Returns the table.
Returns the metatable of an object, or the __metatable field if protected.
Global environment table (a self-reference into the globals table); mutating it changes the global namespace.
Global string with the running language/version; mahina would set its own value.
Interface to the garbage collector. mahina has its own GC, so the option set may differ from Lua's.

Compiles a chunk from a string into a callable (vararg) closure; returns (nil,msg) on syntax error. Deterministic; runtime-compile is a design choice. Subset: string chunk only (no reader fn), no mode/env args.
Writes arguments (via tostring) to stdout, tab-separated, trailing newline. mahina: nativePrint, routed through Vm.out (injectable). The canonical pure-output effect.

Emits a warning from its string args (concatenated) to stderr as one line; a single @-prefixed piece is a control message (@off/@on toggle the system, recognized even while off; unknown @… ignored). Pure host output (Vm.err), NOT a recorded effect — like print. Per-session warn_enabled state, not serialized (5.4).

Reads a file via the injected fs_source seam, compiles it (load path), runs it with no args, returns its results. Raises on read/compile error (unlike loadfile). File content is the EffectKind.file_read effect (recorded/replayed) and is validated as UTF-8 at the host boundary (S-B): non-UTF-8 content raises a catchable error. Installed in every VM, host injects the seam. Subset: path arg only (no stdin).

Reads a file via the injected fs_source seam and compiles it (load path) without running; returns the closure or (nil,msg) on a missing file / syntax error. File content is the EffectKind.file_read effect (recorded/replayed) and is validated as UTF-8 at the host boundary (S-B): non-UTF-8 content raises a catchable error. Installed in every VM, host injects the seam. Subset: path arg only, no mode/env.
Lua or native bodies; a native body runs under a one-line Lua shim so its switches happen from a Lua frame (doc 73).
Switches to the coroutine's own stack (doc 73 P0c); errors return false plus the message.
Raises Lua's messages outside a coroutine and across a Zig frame (doc 73 §6.3).
suspended/running/normal/dead, including the main thread.
A native with its coroutine bound (Native.bound, Lua's C-closure upvalue); results without true, errors raised again at the call with Lua's location (doc 73).
Returns the thread and whether it is the main one.
False on the main thread and below a Zig frame.
Closes a suspended or dead coroutine; refuses a running or normal one.

Removed (design doc 06, S-B): a mahina string is code-point-native, so there is no byte index to return. The role splits: string.codepoint(s,i,j) gives scalar code-point values at character positions, and s:encode() gives the raw UTF-8 bytes as an integer array.
Builds a string from zero or more integer Unicode code-point values (0..0x10FFFF, surrogates rejected), each encoded to UTF-8 (design doc 06, S-B).

mahina (design doc 06, S-B): returns the scalar Unicode code-point values of characters in s between character positions i and j (replaces string.byte). s:codepoint() resolves via the string metatable.

mahina (design doc 06, S-B): s:codes() returns an iterator yielding (characterIndex, codePoint) for each character of s. Indexes by code point, not byte; iterator state lives in a serialisable table (the @codes_iter pattern).

mahina extension (design doc 06, S-A): interprets a byte array (table of integers 0..255) as text, returning the interned string; raises a catchable error on invalid UTF-8. The fallible text<-bytes boundary; no Lua 5.4 equivalent.

mahina extension (design doc 06, S-A): a string's UTF-8 bytes as a byte array (table, integer keys 1..n). Total (a string is always valid UTF-8); s:encode() resolves via the string metatable. The text->bytes boundary; no Lua 5.4 equivalent.

Searches s for a pattern; returns start/end indices and captures, or nil. plain disables magic. Code-point-native since design doc 06, S-D: matches by code point and accepts/returns 1-based CHARACTER indices (init, start/end), so find composes with code-point-indexed sub; classes/bracket sets stay ASCII. JIT: records on-trace as a guarded callout (sfindp/smatch, doc 30) — str_find_match runs with zero recording aborts.

Returns a formatted string using printf-style directives plus Lua extensions (%q, %s, etc.). Follows Lua 5.4's str_format: per-conversion spec checks, %a/%A, %q of every literal type; %c writes a code point as UTF-8 and %p the object's stable id.

Returns an iterator yielding successive pattern matches/captures over the string. Code-point-native since design doc 06, S-D: the scan advances by code point and position captures () are CHARACTER indices; classes stay ASCII. JIT: the ITERATION records on-trace (sgmatch composite op + sgm_setpos deferred cursor store, doc 30) and the for-in loop compiles native; the gmatch() constructor call itself stays a barrier by design.

Returns a copy of s with up to n pattern occurrences replaced (string/number/table/function replacement, the last via Vm.callValue); also returns the count. Code-point-native since design doc 06, S-D: empty/non-match advances by a whole code point (never splits a UTF-8 sequence) and position captures () passed to a function replacement are CHARACTER indices; classes stay ASCII.
Returns the number of Unicode code points in the string (same as #). Code-point-native since design doc 06, S-B; O(1) via the cached cp_len.
Returns a copy with uppercase letters lowercased (Unicode simple 1:1 case mapping, pinned unicode_version; ASCII fast path).

Returns the captures (or whole match) of the first pattern occurrence in s, or nil. Code-point-native since design doc 06, S-D: matches by code point, init is a 1-based CHARACTER index, and position captures () are CHARACTER indices; classes stay ASCII. JIT: records on-trace as a guarded callout (smatch + scap_str/scap_int projections, doc 30).
Returns the string repeated n times, optionally joined by a separator.
Returns the string with its code points reversed (each UTF-8 sequence emitted as a unit, so multibyte characters survive). Code-point-native since design doc 06, S-B.
Returns the substring of s from character position i to j (negative indices count from the end). Code-point-native since design doc 06, S-B; the [i,j] character range maps to UTF-8 byte boundaries.
Returns a copy with lowercase letters uppercased (Unicode simple 1:1 case mapping, pinned unicode_version; ASCII fast path).
Serialises values into a binary string per a format string of size/endianness codes.
Returns the byte size of a fixed-size string.pack format.
Deserialises values from a binary string per a format; also returns the next position.
Emits a function's bytecode for reloading. mahina has its own bytecode/IR; serialising it is determinism- and security-hostile.
No utf8 module in mahina (design doc 06, S-B): strings are code-point-native, so this is absorbed into string.char (which already takes code-point integers and UTF-8-encodes them).
No utf8 module (design doc 06): a pattern to match one UTF-8 sequence is meaningless when a string is a sequence of code points; iterating characters is s:codes().
No utf8 module (design doc 06): absorbed into s:codes(), which yields (characterIndex, codePoint) — character indices, not byte positions.
No utf8 module (design doc 06): absorbed into string.codepoint, which takes character positions (not byte positions) and returns scalar code-point values.
No utf8 module (design doc 06): a string's code-point count is just #s / string.len. There is no invalid-byte case — every mahina string is valid UTF-8 by construction.
No utf8 module (design doc 06): byte<->character offset conversion is not meaningful when indices are already code points. Raw bytes are reached via s:encode().
Concatenates array elements list[i..j] into a string separated by sep.
Inserts value at position pos (default: end), shifting later elements up.
Removes and returns the element at pos (default: last), shifting later elements down.
Copies a1[f..e] into a2 starting at index t (handles overlapping ranges).
Returns a new table holding all args in its array part plus an 'n' count field.
Returns list[i..j] as multiple return values (inverse of table.pack).

Sorts the list in place using < or a comparator (called via Vm.callValue). Heapsort — deterministic, O(n log n) worst case, terminates under an inconsistent comparator; not stable and we do not emulate Lua's invalid-order-function detection.
Returns the absolute value of x, preserving integer/float subtype.
Returns the smallest integer not less than x.
Returns the largest integer not greater than x.
Returns the remainder of x/y rounding the quotient toward zero (C fmod).
Returns the integral and fractional parts of x as two values.
Returns the square root of x.
Returns e raised to the power x.
Returns the logarithm of x in the given base (default natural log).
Returns the sine of x (radians).
Returns the cosine of x (radians).
Returns the tangent of x (radians).
Returns the arc sine of x (radians).
Returns the arc cosine of x (radians).
Returns atan(y/x) using both signs to pick the quadrant (x defaults to 1).
Converts x from radians to degrees.
Converts x from degrees to radians.
Returns the maximum of its numeric arguments.
Returns the minimum of its numeric arguments.
Returns x as an integer if exactly representable, else nil/fail.
Returns 'integer'/'float'/nil for the number subtype of x.
Returns whether integer m < n when both are read as unsigned.
The constant pi.
Positive infinity (HUGE_VAL).
The maximum representable integer value.
The minimum representable integer value.

math.random()=float[0,1); math.random(n)=int[1,n] (n==0=full-width int); math.random(m,n)=int[m,n] (m>n errors). Uniform via own Mersenne-rejection projectU64 on the pinned Xoshiro256 (Lua-shaped, not PUC-stream-compatible). Seed is the recorded .random_seed effect for replay.
math.randomseed(x)=deterministic re-seed (no effect); math.randomseed()=fresh OS-entropy seed via the .random_seed record/replay effect. Single u64 seed (Xoshiro256); returns the seed used.

Monotonic time in seconds as a float since the VM got its clock (Vm.setClockSource), not CPU time (nativeClock), namespaced under os; tagged EffectKind.clock (the recorded result is now the float), routed through the injected ClockSource. mahina extension os.nsclock() returns the raw integer nanoseconds (shares the .clock effect). ClockUnavailable with no source.
mahina extension: monotonic integer nanoseconds from the same clock source as os.clock (shares the .clock effect). Clock group.

Current time (wall_clock effect, integer seconds), or the instant a date table names in local time, normalized in place like mktime; the zone is the local_zone effect (offset, DST flag, abbreviation; doc 65 §8). Lua's field errors. isdst mismatches approximate glibc's search with half-year probes (stdlib/os.zig). Time group.
strftime in the C locale (datetime.zig, every C99 conversion; Lua's checkoption) or a '*t' table; '!' is UTC with no host input, otherwise one local_zone effect. Time group.
Returns t2 - t1 in seconds. Both are required integer timestamps, as in Lua 5.4. Pure arithmetic over timestamps; no host call.
Returns the value of an environment variable, or nil. Nondeterministic input; log-outputs effect. Env group (doc 65).

Returns a table of every environment variable of the process (name to string), for building a spawned child's env (doc 75 §3.1). Nondeterministic input; one log-outputs effect per call. Not in real Lua.

Ends the program as the non-catchable Error.Exit with Vm.exit_status (true 0, false 1, an integer as given); the CLI exits with it, the C API returns MH_EXIT (mh_exit_status, Rust Error::Exit). Logs nothing; 'close' has nothing to do. Env group (doc 65 §7).
Deletes a file or empty directory through the host (fs_mutate effect); failures raise or return nil, msg, code (--lua-io-errors). Files group.
Renames a file or directory through the host (fs_mutate effect); failures raise or return nil, msg, code. Files group.
Creates an empty file in the temporary directory and returns its name (fs_tmpname effect); raises 'unable to generate a unique filename' on failure, as Lua does. Files group.
Runs a command via the OS shell. Process spawning: nondeterministic and unsandboxable; forbidden.
Sets/queries the C locale per category. Mutable global locale breaks reproducibility; mahina fixes locale semantics.

Opens a file in a mode (r/w/a, +, b), returning a handle. Files group (doc 65). The id is a VM counter; the result is a file_open effect. Raises on failure (nil, msg, code under --lua-io-errors). b mode reads and writes byte arrays.
Closes a file (default: current output file). stdio or files group. Standard streams refuse ('cannot close standard file'). file_control effect.
Reads from the default input per the formats (l/L/n/a/count). stdio or files group. One file_read_op effect per format; text counts are code points (doc 65 Q2); stdout is flushed before a stdin read.
Writes string/number args to the default output file; returns the file. Installed in every VM: stdout/stderr write to the output seam and are not effects; a file write is a file_write effect.
Iterator reading successive lines/formats from a file (default input without a name), closing a file it opened at EOF. stdio or files group. No to-be-closed 4th-value semantics (no __close).
Sets (by name or handle) or returns the default input file. stdio or files group; a keyframe root.
Sets (by name or handle) or returns the default output file. stdio or files group; a keyframe root.
Flushes the default output file. Installed in every VM; stdout flushes the output seam (fully buffered when not a terminal, doc 65 §6), a file flush is a file_control effect.
Returns a handle to an auto-removed temporary file, opened text-mode w+. Files group; file_open effect.
Returns 'file'/'closed file'/nil for a candidate handle. Pure; installed in every VM.
Predefined handle for standard input; the default input. stdio group.
Predefined handle for standard output (the VM's output seam); the default output. Every VM. Not seekable; takes no byte arrays.
Predefined handle for standard error (the VM's error seam). Every VM.
Runs a program in a separate process, connected by a pipe. Process spawning; forbidden like os.execute.
Method: reads using the formats (l/L/n/a/count; b mode: count/a into byte arrays). One file_read_op effect per format.
Method: writes strings/numbers (b mode: also byte arrays); returns the file. file_write effect for files.
Method: returns an iterator over the file per the formats (default l); does not close the file.
Method: gets/sets the byte position relative to set/cur/end; file_seek effect. stdout/stderr and pipes are not seekable.
Method: flushes the file's buffered output; file_control effect for files.
Method: sets buffering mode (no/full/line) and optional size; stdout switches the CLI's stdout buffering; file_control effect for files.
Method: closes the file handle (standard streams refuse); file_control effect.

mahina extension (doc 73 §7.6): starts a sleep of s seconds and returns it as a pending task to await (gives nothing). Clock group; installed only with an async host (Vm.enableAio: the CLI's worker-thread host, or a replay). Each completion is an aio_complete + aio_result effect, so a replay wakes tasks in the recorded order and never sleeps.

mahina extension (doc 73 §7.6): reads a whole file on a host worker thread; the await gives its contents, a string that must be valid UTF-8, or a byte array with "b". Files group, async host only. A failure raises at the await (nil, msg, code under --lua-io-errors).
mahina extension (doc 73 §7.6): replaces a file with a string, number or byte array on a host worker thread; the await gives true. Files group, async host only; failures as aio.read.

mahina extension (doc 73 §7.6): adds a string, number or byte array at the end of a file (creating it) on a host worker thread; the await gives true. Files group, async host only; failures as aio.read.

Loads a module by name via the searchers, running it once and caching in package.loaded. Built on the injectable fs_source + file_read effect, so a game/embedding host gets it for free and it record/replays deterministically.
Table of already-loaded modules keyed by name; require consults and populates it. Pre-seeded with the built-in module tables (_G, package, string, table, math, os, io).
Table of loader functions tried by the first built-in searcher before the path searcher.
Search-path template for module source (default ./?.mah;./?/init.mah;./?.lua;./?/init.lua); the path searcher walks it via the file_read effect.
Inert empty field kept only for script compatibility — mahina has no native (C) module loading under determinism, so there is no cpath searcher.
Constant string describing path-handling configuration (separators and marks).
Ordered array of searcher functions require tries: built-in preload + path searchers (manual natives, rebound by name on snapshot restore); a host may prepend/replace its own.
Searches a ;-separated path template for a (dot-mapped) module name via the file_read effect; returns the first readable path or (nil, tried-paths).
Dynamically links a C library and returns a function from it. No sandbox/determinism guarantee; forbidden.
Returns a string traceback of the call stack, optionally prefixed by a message (a non-string message passes through unchanged); honours an optional level. No thread argument (no coroutines).
Returns info about a function or stack level. Reflection superseded by the trace visualiser; breaks abstraction.
Returns the name/value of a local at a stack level. Reflection; use the trace visualiser instead.
Assigns a local at a stack level. Mutating reflection; breaks the deterministic model.
Returns the name/value of a function upvalue. Reflection; superseded by the visualiser.
Sets a function upvalue. Mutating reflection; forbidden.
Returns a unique id for an upvalue cell. Implementation-internal reflection.
Makes one closure's upvalue share another's cell. Implementation-internal mutation.
Returns a value's metatable ignoring __metatable protection. Use the basic getmetatable.
Sets the metatable of any-typed value. Bypasses protection; use the basic setmetatable.
Returns the implementation's internal registry table. Implementation-internal.
Returns a userdata's n-th user value. C-userdata reflection; out of scope.
Sets a userdata's n-th user value. C-userdata reflection; out of scope.
Returns the current debug hook. Hook machinery superseded by the trace recorder.
Installs a per-call/return/line/count hook. Conflicts with the JIT and trace recorder; forbidden.
Enters an interactive debug REPL. Superseded by the time-travel visualiser.
